name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3443
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Novel written by Venus de Milo?

definitions.text: Novel written by Venus de Milo?

blocks.note: surface reading: a book the famous statue might have written
setter's reading: the statue has lost both arms, so her book would bid them goodbye

explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is the armless Greek statue in the Louvre; Hemingway's war novel's title describes her loss literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's 1929 novel is the book, and its title suits an author who has parted with both limbs.

clue.text: Conflict interrupts commercial grant

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so the conflict word sits inside

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks into an advertisement for a funding scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to grant is to bestow or confer something, which is to award it.

clue.text: Handcrafted sitar, retuned by orderly to excess

indicators.note: retuning resets strings into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of sitar, rearranged
slang for fussily, compulsively neat

explanation.surface: A handmade Indian instrument gets retuned by an obsessively tidy musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisanal goods are made by skilled craftspeople, meaning made by hand.

clue.text: Premier of England has garment for getaway

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: opening letter of England
has shortened to 's
a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister keeps a cloak ready for a quick exit.
explanation.walkthrough: Premier looks like the Prime Minister, but it only picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight from danger or capture, which is an escape.

clue.text: Follow tennis rule where every second counts

indicators.note: only every second letter is counted, so alternate letters are kept starting from the second

blocks.note: even-numbered letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Obey the regulation in a tennis match where each second matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards, which means to follow on.

clue.text: Using the same characters, ignited an epoch and an unfinished epoch

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: lit means set alight
an era is an epoch
an epoch is a time; the last letter goes

explanation.surface: An age was set on fire, along with another age left half done.
explanation.definitionFit: Literatim is Latin for letter by letter, so a copy made literatim keeps every character.

clue.text: Embellish or label New Testament

blocks.note: taken as written
to label something is to name it
NT is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A choice between decorating a Bible or tagging it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to decorate, and to ornament something is to decorate it too.

clue.text: A substance used by fiddlers is made of frog's innards and Kissinger's gut

indicators.note: innards are what lies inside, so the outside letters are dropped
the gut is the middle of a body, so the central letters are taken

blocks.note: inner letters of frog
the three central letters of Kissinger

explanation.surface: Fiddlers' bow resin is supposedly made from a frog's insides and a statesman's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State; the frog is also the part of a violin bow the player holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin violinists rub on their bows for grip on the strings.

clue.text: Kidnappers sent crash out of control

indicators.note: things out of control fly about anyhow, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Abductors drove a car into something after losing control.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers snatch people, so they are body snatchers in the plain sense.

clue.text: Charges a duty for the speaker

indicators.note: what the speaker hears matters, not the spelling, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a duty is a tax, and the phrase 'a tax' spoken runs together

explanation.surface: Someone levies a fee on a person who is giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to rush at an enemy, the same as to attack.

clue.text: Nation is the first to be captivated by fish

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Nation is kept
being held captive means being shut inside, so these letters go within the fish

blocks.note: first part of the fish, a tuna
opening letter of Nation
taken as written
the first in number is one, the Roman numeral I
last letter of tuna, closing around the captives

explanation.surface: A country gets caught by a fish before any other.
explanation.walkthrough: N, IS and I (one, the first) go inside TUNA. Nation does double duty: it is the definition and supplies its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Criticize the musical sense of a piece of software, and vanish

blocks.note: to dis is slang for to criticize
an app is an application program
an ear for music is musical sense

explanation.surface: Pan an app for its poor sound and then delete it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hyper dude I chased originally

indicators.note: originally points to the very start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a dude is a man
taken as written
opening letter of chased

explanation.surface: An overexcited guy was pursued by me at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hyper is wildly overexcited, and manic describes that frenzied energy.

clue.text: Finished 501?

blocks.note: the 500 part: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the 1 part, written as a word

explanation.walkthrough: Split 501 into 500 and 1: D in Roman numerals, then the word ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is complete, the plain meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Baba ghanoush, perhaps, and a bit of hummus on underpants — "like, ew!"

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here just its opening letter

blocks.note: baba ghanoush is an aubergine dip, an example of one
opening letter of hummus
a thong is skimpy underwear

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from Middle Eastern dip smeared on their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two examples: the vowels in 'like' and 'ew' each glide from one sound to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is a vowel sound that slides between two positions, as in the words like and ew.

clue.text: Be patient when discussing heaviness and expanse of water

indicators.note: discussing is talking, so the words are taken as they would be spoken

blocks.note: heaviness is weight
taken as written
a sea is a broad expanse of water

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm while talking about how heavy and wide a body of water is.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait and see is to hold off until events unfold, which is being patient.

clue.text: Butt of a practical joke with food, mostly eaten by a quiet stream

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so these letters go within the stream

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a rill is a small stream
food without its last letter

explanation.surface: The victim of a prank involving food, eaten by a quiet brook.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiet is the musical direction piano, abbreviated p; a rill is a small brook.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is someone tricked by a hoax on the first of April.

clue.text: Revolting sight: pâté and pasta

indicators.note: revolting can mean rising up and overturning order, so these letters are upended

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: A disgusting plate of meat paste served alongside noodles.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting reads as disgusting; it is the signal to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Prude ran, maneuvering like an eagle

indicators.note: maneuvering moves pieces into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A prim person runs off, swooping like a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The eagle is a golf score, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is two strokes fewer than par on a hole, so it is under par.

clue.text: Friend on independent capital: "It's like this puzzle's number"

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
IND is the abbreviation for independent
the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A pal sitting on an independent capital remarks on the puzzle's number.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is No 3443, which reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition gives an example: 3443 reads identically in both directions, the defining trait of a palindrome.

clue.text: Damages a planet

blocks.note: first meaning: spoils or harms
second meaning: the red fourth planet from the sun

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sentence about a world being harmed; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means spoils or blemishes; as a noun it names the fourth planet.

clue.text: Cool "naked brick" material

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: fab, short for fabulous, means great or cool
brick without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A stylish building material that is bare, unclad brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, which is material in the sense of textile.

clue.text: One of señorita's requirements is equality about land's boundaries

indicators.note: about means around, so the equality word wraps the other letters
the boundaries of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters count

blocks.note: a tie is an equal score
outside letters of land

explanation.surface: A young Spanish woman demands equal rights over a territory's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling señorita properly needs the wavy mark over its n, so the mark is one of the word's requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy accent over the n in señorita is a tilde, one thing the word needs to be spelt right.

clue.text: Red Lobster's leader raised a baseball team

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so only the first letter is taken
raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: opening letter of Lobster
a baseball side has nine players and is called a nine

explanation.surface: The boss of the seafood chain Red Lobster lifted up a ball club.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Lobster is a US seafood restaurant chain; Red here is a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolsheviks, and Red is a common term for a communist.

clue.text: Beast, large and green, coming back to swallow funny hat

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the letters are read from right to left
something funny is odd or out of order, so these letters are jumbled
swallowing takes something inside, so the jumbled letters go within

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
green means inexperienced or naive
the letters of hat, jumbled

explanation.surface: A big green monster backs up and gulps down a silly hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both green and large together, before the jumbled hat goes inside; green means naive, inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A leviathan is a huge biblical sea monster, so a beast.

clue.text: Watch Republican abandoning classical poet

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the party member leaving the Roman poet's side.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch, so a watch as a noun.

clue.text: Veto the rise of no crooked politician

indicators.note: a rise in a down clue lifts the word upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: to nix is to veto
taken as written

explanation.surface: Blocking any advancement for a dishonest politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Nixon resigned over Watergate after insisting he was not a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon, the US president forced out by the Watergate scandal, is the archetypal crooked politician.

clue.text: Acknowledge chaotic merger of town and university post office

indicators.note: chaotic means disordered, so the merged letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
PO is the abbreviation for post office

explanation.surface: Admitting a messy amalgamation of a town, a college and its mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess or admit it, an idiom for acknowledging.

clue.text: Al Ritter's 20

blocks.note: Al Gore, the former US vice president
Tex Ritter, the singing cowboy of Western films

explanation.walkthrough: Each first name calls up a famous surname and vice versa: Al Gore and Tex Ritter, joined into the brand name. The definition 20 points to the answer to 20-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore-Tex is a waterproof breathable fabric, which answers 20-down.

clue.text: It involves much counting and relocating components, up to four times each

definitions.text: It involves much counting and relocating components, up to four times each

blocks.note: surface reading: a tally followed by rearranging parts, like an anagram puzzle
setter's reading: rearrange the answer's letters and none appears more than four times; and a national vote involves a big count and moves members of the legislature

explanation.walkthrough: On one reading, votes are counted and seats change hands; on another, the answer's letters, rearranged, use its commonest letter four times.
explanation.definitionFit: A general election is a nationwide vote, with ballots counted and legislators replaced or moved.
